greet.text: An old man in earth-brown robes kneels at a crack in the ridge, pressing the stone shut with two fingers as if closing a wound. 'Mind your step. The mountain is older than my patience, and it has been bleeding since the last war.'

choices.label: Hold the rubble steady while he works. (3 days)
Ask how a cultivator crosses from Nascent Soul to Soul Formation.
Bring the two Soul Infant Fruit Wen asked for.

mending.text: 'Where the old cultivators fought, the veins of the world were cut. Qi leaks out and beasts grow mad on it. I close what I can. It is slow work. Heaven does not grade it, so I grade it myself, and I am a harsh teacher.'

hold.text: The stone is colder than any stone should be and heavier than it looks. When the crack finally seals he sits back and breathes out for what sounds like a century. 'Good hands. Most would have asked what they would be paid.' Mountain-qi settles gently into your bones.

severing.text: 'You cut away the part of yourself that wants to be remembered. A soul that no longer needs a body can no longer be held by one. It is not a victory; it is a sort of generosity. The Spirit Severing Pill only helps those who already know what they are willing to lose. Know that first.'

errand_ask.text: 'The ridge's old wounds drink fruit-spirit the way the dry earth drinks rain. Two Soul Infant Fruit from the Terraces, left to ripen on the stem, if you can find that much luck. I will not pay you in stones. I have a pill a friend once pressed on me, and no more years to need it.'

errand_thanks.text: He turns each fruit over in the light as though it were a sleeping child, then lays them in the crack and the stone closes around them with a sigh. 'Take this. Live a little longer than you planned. The mountain will need more hands.'
